topic: Neuroendocrine and circuit mechanisms of romantic love

accepted_gaps.statement: Operational boundaries among sexual motivation, partner-directed reward, and durable bond maintenance are not unified across species or time.
A common causal protocol has not decomposed the contributions of VTA-NAc dopamine, hypothalamic neuropeptides, and limbic recognition circuits.
The interaction and temporal order of dopamine, oxytocin, vasopressin, sex steroids, and stress hormones remain unresolved.
Human partner-cue imaging and vole receptor perturbation lack a shared cross-species measurement language.
Partner preference is difficult to separate from general social approach, sexual behavior, novelty, locomotion, stress buffering, and nonsocial reward.
Receptor-genetic and endocrine associations need larger preregistered replication and explicit moderator tests.

rejected_or_unresolved_candidates.statement: There is one universal love center.
rejected_or_unresolved_candidates.reason: Contradicted by distributed circuit evidence and insufficiently operational.

rejected_or_unresolved_candidates.statement: One hormone is the love hormone.
rejected_or_unresolved_candidates.reason: Receptor localization, context, and non-specific social effects require a multivariable model.
